title: Hosting SLA evaluation session — hosting vs dedicated vs private
next_steps: Redwood to share per-model streaming perf matrix and test harness link
Schedule 2-hour benchmark pilot for 10k token burst (proposed 2026-10-12)
Send dedicated capacity pricing and reserved commit options
Share SOC2/ISO security packet and network design notes for VPC/private deployment

Maya Chen | Draft pilot run plan and sample workloads | 2026-10-08

summary: Discovery focused on whether BeaconFleet should choose Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private. Primary constraints: p95 latency targets for short streaming responses (<=300ms), sustained concurrency of ~200-300 users with occasional bursts to 1k, and strict data residency/KMS requirements. Agreed next step is a 2-hour benchmark pilot using customer prompts; Redwood to provide perf matrix and test harness.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, I'm Samir from Redwood, joining with Maya our SE and Iris from success. real quick, is the time still good?
[00:09] Eli Moreno (BeaconFleet CTO): Yep, good here, thanks. We wanted to make sure this call covers p95 goals and what you'd recommend for production.
[00:18] Priya Nair (SRE): Hi, Priya here, we'll be pretty technical, hope that's ok. Our main ask: we need predictable p95 for streaming chat responses, basically sub 300ms for short responses — that includes our own network egress, so we want the server side to be conservative.
[00:35] Maya Chen (Redwood SE): Got it, that's helpful. When you say short responses, what's the token range and are you streaming token-by-token or sending a single chunk?
[00:44] Daniel Cho (ML Eng): Mostly streaming, token-by-token for chat UI. Typical reply lengths are 30–120 tokens, median around 50. Occasional longer ones for code or step lists.
[00:52] Samir: Good. And concurrency — what steady-state and what bursts do you expect?
[00:57] Eli: steady-state around 200 active sessions, peaks to maybe 1,000 for campaign events lasting 10–20 minutes.
[01:05] Priya: Also want to understand tail behavior: p95 is fine but we need to quantify p99 and cold starts, we cannot have long tails during events.
[01:13] Maya: Absolutely. For streaming, we typically measure server-side token emission latency and per-token processing. For example on a 70B-ish open model we see server-side per-token generation at X ms depending on quantization and batching — sorry that was vague, let me rephrase with numbers in the follow-up perf matrix.
[01:29] Eli: We also are comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private. Data residency and KMS are must-haves for private, but we prefer hosted if you can hit the latency and cost targets.
[01:38] Samir: Understood. High level: hosted gives fastest time-to-value and dynamic scaling, dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation with reserved commit, private gives full control for KMS/data residency. For your p95 <=300ms target for 50-token responses, hosted is possible if we allocate lower-latency model variants and enable prefix caching. Dedicated helps if you want consistent p95 under sustained load and can commit.
[01:58] Lena Ruiz (Procurement): timeline question, if we go dedicated or private, what's procurement cadence? Any long lead times?
[02:04] Iris Ko (CSM): Dedicated usually has a short onboarding window once contract is in place — provisioning GPUs can take 2–4 weeks depending on region and capacity; private/VPC deployments closer to 4–8 weeks with network config. We'll share a runbook.
[02:16] Daniel: Onbenchmarks — how do you handle token/sec vs latency tradeoffs? We measure end-to-end tokens/sec to our UI and p95 — often increasing batching improves cost but hurts latency.
[02:26] Maya: Right, there's a tradeoff. Redwood has workload-aware batching and continuous batching; you can set a max batch latency to prioritize p95. Also prefix/KV cache reduces repeated compute for similar prompts. In practice, for streaming short replies we tune batch size small and rely on single-request fast paths.
[02:41] [00:02:41] Priya: Curious about the KV cache — if a user asks multiple follow-ups in a session, will cache reduce per-token latency substantially?
[02:49] Maya: Yes, KV cache avoids recomputing past attention for previous tokens when applicable — for a chat history of 200 tokens, subsequent responses can be 2–3x faster. But cache hit rates depend on prompt patterns.
[02:59] Eli: For our campaigns we care about token throughput too; we estimate sustained token/sec at ~4k tokens/sec and burst to 20k tokens/sec during peak minutes. Is that reasonable?
[03:09] Samir: That's in the realm of what Dedicated can deliver with right pooling and autoscaling; hosted can handle bursts but you may see slightly higher p95 under sudden ramps without reserved capacity. We'll propose a pilot to validate.
[03:21] Daniel: On the pilot — can we run our prompt sets? We want to include a mix: short confirmations, multi-step code blocks, and the large summaries ~400 tokens.
[03:30] Maya: Yes, we prefer customer-provided prompts. We'll run a 2-hour pilot with controlled ramp: steady-state then stepped bursts. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, token-emission latency, and cold-starts.
[03:43] [00:03:43] Priya: Network considerations — for private you said VPC peering with direct connect? We need details on egress and NAT.
[03:51] Samir: For private deployments we support customer VPC peering and on-prem options. We integrate with customer KMS (bring your own key) for model request logging encryption. We'll share an architecture sketch; there are tradeoffs: private reduces egress hop but adds ops overhead.
[04:06] Eli: Security: we need SOC2, iso, audit logs and token-level tracing for debugging.
[04:12] Iris: We'll send the security packet. Redwood offers audit logs and token-level cost breakdown in Console; for private deployments we can increase retention.
[04:22] Daniel: How about quantization options — do you run int8 and what hit do you see on latency and quality?
[04:28] Maya: We support a range of quantizations. int8 often yields 2x memory reduction and modest latency improvement on some model families; accuracy impact depends on model. For tight p95 targets we usually recommend low-latency kernel paths and mixed-precision when acceptable. We'll include per-model quantization tradeoffs in the perf matrix.
[04:44] [00:04:44] Priya: Cold-starts: what's a realistic cold-start time for a model ~70B if not warmed and we get a sudden burst?
[04:51] Maya: Cold-starts vary — container spin up could be tens of seconds; model loading and warm-up maybe 30–90s depending on infra and quantization. That's why we recommend warm pools or reserved capacity for predictable events.
[05:03] Eli: That matches our concern. For the big campaign we want near-zero cold starts. So likely dedicated with warm pools.
[05:10] Samir: Exactly. Dedicated reserved pools let you keep warm instances and autoscale within a guaranteed capacity. Also automatic fallback to smaller model variants if capacity is constrained.
[05:19] Daniel: On fallback — what's the developer experience? Can we pin a model and have automatic degrade to a quantized variant?
[05:25] Maya: Yes, rollouts and fallback policies let you pin primary model and list variants; requests can route to a qual-checked fallback. We log degraded responses so you can track quality regressions.
[05:35] [00:05:35] Priya: For the pilot, what metrics should we capture? We want token emission latency, end-to-end p95, p99, cold-start frequency, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost per 1k tokens.
[05:46] Samir: Agreed. We'll capture those. We'll also produce a CSV with per-request latencies and a dashboard link.
[05:53] Lena: Procurement question: if we do dedicated reserved, how soft is the commit, and are there annual discounts?
[05:59] Iris: Reserved commits are typically 6 or 12 month; discounts scale with volume. We'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up doc.
[06:07] Eli: Any gotchas with multi-region? We need Europe and US presence, and traffic routed by latency.
[06:13] Maya: Multi-region is supported; Smart routing routes by policy (latency, cost, region) and can failover. There's also cross-region caching considerations. We'll detail best practices.
[06:26] [00:06:26] Daniel: About measurement methodology — we will want both server-side and client-side measurements. Does Redwood provide a test harness?
[06:33] Samir: Yes, we'll share a test harness link. It runs head-to-head tests and collects server and client telemetry. We'll also include scripts to replay your prompt sets.
[06:41] Priya: For the pilot's scale, can Redwood simulate 1k concurrent sessions with streaming?
[06:46] Maya: We can run scaled pilots; we recommend a staged ramp so we can capture tail latency. We'll coordinate rate generators.
[06:54] Eli: Ok that sounds good. On the security docs, please include the KMS integration flow and where keys live in private deployments.
[07:01] Iris: noted, we'll attach that.
[07:05] [00:07:05] Samir: Quick recap — Redwood provides hosted for immediate usage, dedicated for predictable p95 under sustained load with warm pools, and private for strict residency/KMS. Pilot plan: 2-hour bench with your prompts, ramp and bursts, we'll deliver a perf matrix and recommendations. Next step dates: we'll send perf matrix by 10/6, pilot 10/12, pricing by 10/8.
[07:22] Eli: Great. Couple more quick clarifs — what's the typical per-token cost delta hosted vs dedicated for the same model?
[07:30] Iris: Hosted is usage-based; dedicated unit costs are lower but require commit. We'll send concrete numbers in pricing.
[07:36] Daniel: Are there any limitations around streaming APIs such as idle timeouts or connection limits?
[07:42] Maya: There are reasonable timeouts; connection quotas exist per-tenant but can be increased for dedicated/private. We'll include defaults in the docs.
[07:50] [00:07:50] Priya: One last thing: observability — can we get per-route latency and token breakdown so product owners can tie cost to features?
[07:57] Samir: Yes, Console gives per-route/per-model dashboards and token-level cost traces.
[08:03] Eli: Alright thanks everyone, we'll look for the docs.
[08:07] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with the perf matrix, security packet and pilot plan.
[08:12] [00:08:12] (call ends)
notes: Transcript has occasional mis-attributions and minor transcription errors (product names and acronyms). Customer is strongly leaning Dedicated for campaign events due to cold-start and p95 concerns but remains open to Hosted if pilots show adequate tail behavior.
